Tail Probabilities on the Log Scale

Source: R/utility_functions.R
tail_helpers.Rd

Three internal helpers serve the distribution and quantile functions of the families with a closed form. log1mexp_neg() computes \(\log(1 - e^a)\) for \(a \le 0\), through log(-expm1(a)) when \(a > -\log 2\) and through log1p(-exp(a)) otherwise, so that the result keeps its relative accuracy at both ends (Maechler, 2012). cdf_from_log_tails() returns the probability that lower.tail and log.p select from the logarithms of the two tails, and the caller computes both logarithms. quantile_log_tails() converts a probability given with lower.tail and log.p into the logarithms of the lower and the upper tail, without forming \(1 - p\) or exponentiating a logarithm; a probability outside \([0, 1]\) gives NaN for both.

Usage

log1mexp_neg(a)

cdf_from_log_tails(log_lower, log_upper, lower.tail, log.p)

quantile_log_tails(p, lower.tail, log.p)

Arguments

a

A numeric vector of non-positive numbers.

log_lower, log_upper

Numeric vectors, the logarithms of \(P(Y \le q)\) and \(P(Y > q)\).

lower.tail, log.p

Logical of length 1, with the meaning that they have in distrib_cdf() and distrib_quantile().

p

A numeric vector of probabilities, or of their logarithms when log.p = TRUE.

Value

log1mexp_neg() and cdf_from_log_tails() return a numeric vector of the length of their input; quantile_log_tails() returns a list with the numeric vectors lower and upper.

References

Maechler, M. (2012). Accurately computing \(\log(1 - \exp(-|a|))\). Vignette of the R package Rmpfr.

Examples

# The helper keeps the digits that the direct formula loses (it gives -Inf).
distributions7:::log1mexp_neg(-1e-20)
#> [1] -46.0517
log(1 - exp(-1e-20))
#> [1] -Inf

# The upper tail is computed for a probability given on the log scale.
distributions7:::quantile_log_tails(log(1e-30), lower.tail = FALSE,
                                    log.p = TRUE)
#> $lower
#> [1] -1e-30
#> 
#> $upper
#> [1] -69.07755
#>
